newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu cancels U.S. trip, Hebron clashes end.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu cancels U.S. trip, Hebron clashes end.

text.p: Clashes erupted in the West Bank town of Hebron on Saturday as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cancelled a U.S. trip in a move local media attributed to the peacemaking crisis with Palestinians.
Netanyahu's spokesmen denied the faltering peace process was the reason for the cancellation.

In Hebron, Israeli troops firing rubber bullets shot and wounded 30 Palestinians, witnesses said. The Israeli army confirmed the clashes but said it did not know of casualties. The demonstrators withdrew after several hours of fighting.

Earlier on Saturday, Palestinian gunmen shot and wounded an Israeli woman motorist at Har Adar Jewish settlement in the West Bank north of Jerusalem, Israeli security sources said. The army said it arrested six suspects from the Arab village of Biddu.
The Palestinian Authority cabinet said in a statement issued on Saturday after its weekly meeting late on Friday:

"The Palestinian public were patient for a long time over the accelerating Israeli trespasses and violations and Netanyahu's affirmations on continuing the settlement attacks. They cannot be patient anymore."

Tensions between Israel and the Palestinians have been high and periodically flared into violence since Israel began building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March. Peace negotiations came to a halt after building began.

A former Israeli peace negotiator told Israel Television on Saturday that the "zig-zag" manner in which Netanyahu was dealing with the Palestinians in peace talks had worn away their trust and was the principal reason for the peacemaking freeze.

"If this freeze continues...I certainly am talking about the winds of war. I think we are talking about an uprising in the territories which is violent and armed," Oren Shahor, who recently retired from the Israeli army, added.

Shahor, a major-general, headed Israel's team in talks on civilian issues with the Palestinians under Netanyahu and the prime minister's predecessors, Yitzhak Rabin and Shimon Peres of the dovish opposition Labour party Netanyahu ousted a year ago.
Netanyahu suspended Shahor from the peace talks in November after the general met Peres behind his back.

Netanyahu spokesman Ofir Akunis told Reuters Netanyahu's U.S. trip had been cancelled because the prime minister wanted to be in Israel to deal with pending sensitive legislation on who may perform conversions to Judaism in Israel.
Israel's army radio said Netanyahu cancelled because he had hoped for a meeting with President Bill Clinton but now wanted to avoid talks with Clinton due to the faltering peace process.
"That (legislation) is the official excuse...The problem is that the diplomatic process is deadlocked and strongly deadlocked," the radio's diplomatic reporter Udi Segal said.
Netanyahu aide Shai Bazak denied the radio report.

On Thursday, Egyptian envoy Osama el-Baz shuttled between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in his latest bid to solve the impasse. He returned to Egypt saying more work was needed to end the crisis.
Palestinians demand Israel halt settlement construction before they will resume substantive negotiations. Netanyahu vows to continue building.

Several Palestinian demonstrators in Hebron told Reuters they had come to confront the Israelis to protest a non-binding U.S. House of Representatives resolution on Tuesday saying Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital.
The Palestinian cabinet statement said of the House move: "This is a dangerous decision harming the U.S.A.'s credibility and role (as peace talks sponsor)".
Palestinians say settlement building pre-empts final peace talks to be held on issues including Jerusalem's status. They want Arab East Jerusalem as capital of a future state.
Israel vows never to cede any part of the city. It captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East war and annexed it in a move unrecognised by the international community.
